topic.title: Data Handling and Your Responsibilities
topic.shortdesc: Learn where your content goes during translation and what to review before you commit translated files.

body.p: Translation in is a reviewed, reversible workflow. The agent proposes translated files in your workspace, and nothing becomes part of your project until you commit it. The sections below explain where your content goes and what to review before you commit the changes.

section.title: Where Your Content Goes
section.p: To translate content, sends the relevant source content to an AI provider that performs the translation. This means that, during a translation job, the content leaves the infrastructure. The provider operates under terms that require zero data retention, so it does not keep your content for its own use after the request is completed.
Your Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is the authoritative source for how your data is processed.

section.title: Translations Are Proposed Changes to Review
section.p: Like any translation, whether created by a human or by a machine, a translated file can contain errors, including wording that changes the intended meaning. treats translated files like any other proposed change. They are added to your workspace for review before you commit them.
You are responsible for reviewing and verifying translated content before you publish it. See Reviewing Translations Before You Commit for guidance on how to review translations effectively.

section.title: Review the Full Set of Changed Files
section.p: Because translation works by writing files into your workspace, a translation job can potentially change more than just the translated text. When you review the output of a translation job, inspect the complete set of changed files, not only the translated topics. Watch for changes beyond the translation itself, such as changes to publishing templates, build or tool configuration, or markup that affects the published output.

This is the same review practice you would apply to any external contribution to your repository: read the changed files before committing them. Because the changes appear as ordinary workspace edits, you can inspect, modify, or discard any of them before they become part of your project.
